prompt.context:
A bank has a loan-issuing operation that requires the following steps: (1) The loan application is generated at a branch office. (2) A complete applicant background check is performed at the branch office. (3) The application and background check are sent to a loan processing office. (4) The background check is updated and verified at the processing office (this takes much less time than the original check). (5) The loan is either approved or denied.

The bank is considering getting rid of the first background check and only relying on the loan processor's check to speed the process. If the loan processor does the whole check with the proposed new software system, the check takes one additional hour per application at the processor's office.

Key facts:
- Average profit margin for a 'good' loan (loans which are repaid): $0.20 per dollar loaned
- Average marginal loss for a 'bad' loan (loans which are not repaid): $0.50 per dollar loaned
- 50% of applicants pass the first background check
- 90% pass the second background check
prompt.question: Should the bank implement the revised system (eliminating the branch-level background check and relying solely on an enhanced processor-level check)?

clarifying_info.q: How many loan applications are submitted per year?
What is the average value per loan?
What is the default rate under the original system?
What are the processing costs under the original system?
What is the acceptance rate under the original system?
clarifying_info.a: 45% (50% pass the first check, then 90% of those pass the second check: 50% x 90% = 45%)

clarifying_info.q: What is the estimated default rate under the proposed system?
clarifying_info.a: 5% of approved loans (estimated, due to better upfront screening)

clarifying_info.q: What are the processing costs under the proposed system?
clarifying_info.a: $60 per hour, with 1 additional hour per application at the processor's office, plus $50 per application for additional system costs

clarifying_info.q: What is the expected acceptance rate under the proposed system?

framework: Calculate total annual profit under the Original System
Calculate total annual profit under the Proposed System
Compare profits and assess qualitative factors (transition costs, upside risks)

questions.prompt: Calculate annual profit under the Original System
questions.guidance: Compute dollars loaned, then apply the net revenue rate (90% good x $0.20 minus 10% bad x $0.50), then subtract processing costs. A strong answer identifies all three components cleanly before multiplying.

math.setup: 1000 applications x 45% acceptance x $10,000 per loan = total dollars loaned. Net revenue rate = (90% x $0.20) - (10% x $0.50). Profit = (Dollars loaned x Net revenue rate) - (Processing cost x Applications).

questions.prompt: Calculate annual profit under the Proposed System
questions.guidance: Compute dollars loaned at the new acceptance rate, apply the improved net revenue rate (95% good x $0.20 minus 5% bad x $0.50), then subtract both processing components. A strong answer notes that the lower default rate improves per-dollar revenue even though fewer loans are issued.

math.setup: 1000 applications x 40% acceptance x $10,000 per loan = total dollars loaned. Net revenue rate = (95% x $0.20) - (5% x $0.50). Total costs = (processing fee + additional costs) x applications.

questions.prompt: Compare the two systems and make a recommendation
questions.guidance: The proposed system yields $550,000 vs $485,000, an improvement of $65,000. A strong answer recommends proceeding but flags transition costs (retraining, software installation) and potential upside (faster processing attracting more applicants). The candidate should not conclude definitively without acknowledging these qualitative factors.

math.setup: Incremental profit = Proposed profit - Original profit
math.answer: Proposed system is $65,000 more profitable per year before one-time transition costs

recommendation: Based on the model, the bank should implement the proposed system: it generates $550,000 in annual profit versus $485,000 under the current system, an increase of $65,000 per year
The improved loan quality (5% vs 10% default rate) more than compensates for the lower acceptance rate (40% vs 45%) and modestly higher per-application cost ($110 vs $100)
risks: One-time transition costs (employee retraining, software installation, process change management) could erode near-term gains
The 5% default rate and 40% acceptance rate for the proposed system are estimates; actual outcomes may differ
Eliminating the branch-level check may reduce customer satisfaction if applicants dislike fewer touchpoints or longer wait at the processing office
next_steps: Quantify one-time implementation costs to determine payback period
Pilot the new system in a subset of branches before full rollout
Monitor default rates and acceptance rates post-implementation to validate assumptions
Assess whether faster loan processing could increase applicant volume, which would further improve economics
